scope: Decide the stress architecture and publishable whole-word pronunciation policy after B1-B3. Do not change segment identities, romanization, DAYI semantics, morphology, grammar or curriculum in this gate.

inputs.B1: G40=/y/ vowel affirmed; G16=/j/ remains distinct.
inputs.B2: Adjacent vowel sequences, including VVV, are allowed.
inputs.B3: Adjacent vowels remain distinct nuclei by default in careful pronunciation; no automatic /y/->/j/ and no productive diphthong inventory.

options.description: Do not invent a universal fixed stress rule. Treat lexical stress as an explicit word-level property when governed; forms lacking an approved stress value remain publishable only in broad unstressed/syllabic notation, not with a canonical stressed IPA claim.
options.rationale: No historical or governed global stress rule was recovered. This preserves the audited corpus without forcing a new universal prosodic law and allows stress to be added deliberately per lexeme or by a later evidence-backed rule.

options.description: Adopt penultimate stress as a new HNK-wide authored rule, explicitly as design rather than historical recovery.
options.risk: Creates a global prosodic rule without recovered support and may conflict with creator-intended pronunciations of existing forms.

options.description: Adopt initial stress as a new HNK-wide authored rule, explicitly as design rather than historical recovery.
options.risk: Creates a global prosodic rule without recovered support.

options.description: Do not define even a lexical-marking architecture yet; keep all stress unspecified.
options.risk: Preserves uncertainty but blocks a clean path to publishable word pronunciations.

boundary: A broad unstressed form such as /da.y.i/ records segmental nuclei and syllabic planning only; it must not be presented as a complete canonical stressed pronunciation until a stress value is separately governed.
